Former DEA Special Agent Chris Feistl sits down with VladTV to trace his path from a quiet Pennsylvania childhood to the front lines of the cocaine trade in Miami and Colombia. Portrayed in Season 3 of Netflix’s *Narcos*, Feistl explains how a summer police job pushed him toward the DEA, the 17-week academy at Quantico, and undercover work during the Miami Vice and Cocaine Cowboys era.

He breaks down how informants helped agents infiltrate Colombian trafficking networks, the risks cooperators faced from the Cali Cartel, and why transportation was a major weakness for cocaine organizations moving loads into South Florida. Feistl also discusses Operation Cornerstone, the massive 12-ton cocaine seizure hidden in concrete fence posts from Venezuela, as well as corruption cases involving DEA agents in Miami. The conversation touches on Pablo Escobar’s aftermath, Griselda Blanco’s era, undercover strategy, and the realities behind drug war mythology.

In this VladTV interview, Marlow Bates gives a raw firsthand account of violent prison politics and the consequences of reputation behind bars. Speaking with Vlad, Bates describes how word reached him through his wife that another inmate was allegedly claiming they had a beef, leading to a confrontation in the gym involving a hidden knife, administrative annex inmates, and a chaotic response from guards. He also reflects on later run-ins, including seeing the same inmate months afterward and another prison dispute over weed being bagged for sales. Timmirror adds context, noting that street conflicts and “rap buddy” issues continued inside, which is why some details remain off-limits. This clip explores prison survival, inmate hierarchy, retaliation, and how outside conversations could trigger serious consequences inside the walls.

--------
In this raw VladTV interview, John Franzese Jr. reflects on the devastating 1990 death of his sister Gia from a cocaine overdose while he was battling his own addiction. He recounts opening a pizzeria on 62nd and First, relapsing into drinking and drugs, and receiving Gia’s final call while he was smoking crack and spiraling in a New York apartment. Franzese also shares how he learned of her death days later, how Danny Pierson eventually found him at the Queens Theater on Jamaica Avenue, and why the tragedy still didn’t stop his substance abuse.

Franzese details his progression from injecting cocaine to smoking crack after a chance encounter with a kid from Greenpoint, explaining how crack became a substitute when needles were no longer an option. The conversation touches on addiction, family guilt, Gia’s fiancé Michael Suibhne, Israel, and the harsh reality of drugs and alcohol.

In this VladTV interview, Tito “TJ” Dominguez reflects on his 1991 guilty plea for cocaine and marijuana distribution and money laundering, which led to a 13-year federal prison sentence. Dominguez discusses being indicted in the Bahamas, the pressure to plead guilty, and the deaths of associates in boating and airplane accidents that authorities tried to connect to him. He also addresses accusations that he ordered a hit on a federal judge, stressing he was never charged, and recounts how buying a helicopter to escape prison worsened his situation.

Dominguez details spending roughly two and a half years in solitary confinement, describing the psychological toll, limited calls, no visits, and harsh prison conditions. He also shares a striking exchange with a guard who later said their conversation pushed him to leave federal prison work for the Miami Beach Police Department.

--------
Charleston White sits down with VladTV to address online rumors, family allegations, and the real-world impact of scammers using his name. White denies a claim involving a distant cousin, saying the timeline doesn’t add up and referencing San Antonio, Fayetteville, the University of Arkansas, Texas law, and the Bill Cosby case while discussing statutes of limitations and why serious accusations should go to police, not YouTube.

The conversation then turns to a major warning for fans: White says he has not had a Facebook page in over three years, despite a page with over 1 million followers allegedly impersonating him and scamming people through fake bookings, Cash App requests, and bogus “manager” messages. He also talks about being repeatedly deleted from Facebook, mentions Mark Zuckerberg, and explains his business rule: verify through his agent and speak to him directly before sending money.
